reason: Returning cold clouds to the dense disk directly addresses whether expelled gas can make stars again.
expectation: The returning gas may join the disk and form new stars, though it may need to gather or cool further.

alternatives.reason: Feeding the black hole addresses the other goal, but I will follow the star-forming route first.

effect: The returning clouds formed stars in the central disk, completing the first goal.
reaction: Satisfying to see the expelled gas make stars after its return.
reason: The remaining goal asks whether returning gas can feed the black hole again.
expectation: Some returning gas may enter a disk around the black hole and feed it, though not necessarily all of it will cross the horizon.

effect: Another portion of the returning gas supplied a bright disk around the same black hole, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The return to the same central source makes a satisfying conclusion to the outflow’s journey.

mostWorthwhile.text: Returning the clouds to the central disk was most worthwhile: it showed that expelled gas could still form stars.

leastWorthwhile.text: Neither action was notably confusing, though the two short routes made the chapter feel somewhat predictable.

surprise.text: The returning gas could both form stars and feed a bright disk around the same black hole.

arbitrary.text: Neither chosen action felt arbitrary; each corresponded directly to a stated goal.

continue.text: I would continue: following the same material through an outflow and back to two different destinations was satisfying.
